builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
summary: The technique replaces either pooling raw patient-level EHR records across institutions (often legally infeasible) or iterative federated averaging, by having each site transmit only aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary that a central server combines in a single non-iterative step. The cost is modest locally (one spectral decomposition per site plus small-summary communication), but it requires implementing a custom spectral estimator with row-normalization, which is substantial statistical engineering effort outside standard ML frameworks. It can fail when the paper's regularity conditions are violated, when site populations are strongly heterogeneous so a shared low-rank structure is a poor assumption, or when summary statistics inadvertently leak information despite the privacy motivation.
rationale: The method targets privacy-constrained multi-institutional EHR analysis, a specialized statistical setting that does not intersect with the reader's LLM inference, fine-tuning, or agent production workload unless they specifically operate in federated healthcare analytics.
technique: Non-iterative federated spectral decomposition for EHR embeddings

claims.statement: The technique replaces either pooling raw patient-level EHR records across institutions (often legally infeasible) or iterative federated averaging, by having each site transmit only aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary that a central server combines in a single non-iterative step. The cost is modest locally (one spectral decomposition per site plus small-summary communication), but it requires implementing a custom spectral estimator with row-normalization, which is substantial statistical engineering effort outside standard ML frameworks. It can fail when the paper's regularity conditions are violated, when site populations are strongly heterogeneous so a shared low-rank structure is a poor assumption, or when summary statistics inadvertently leak information despite the privacy motivation.

Simulations show the method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across data settings; no multiplicative factor is reported.
